his_statement: π₁(U) … isomorphisme ?
statement: For any proper normal model X, does its regular locus U already have the birational fundamental group; equivalently, can every finite étale cover of U become étale on some proper modification?
status_on_pages: open on the pages; false in this generality
computation: Field invariants, valuation, quotient singularities and regular-locus hypotheses checked in independent_checks.md §4; algebraic substitutions in checks.py.
fate: A complex projective quotient X=(P¹×P¹)/⟨(x,y)↦(−x,−y)⟩ has four isolated quotient singularities. Its regular locus has a connected étale double cover from the complement of the fixed points. Writing the invariant field as C(a,t), a=x², t=y/x, the extension C(x,y)/C(a,t) ramifies at the a-adic valuation. That valuation has a centre on every proper model, so the cover cannot extend étale on any of them. A regular proper rational model has trivial π₁. This independently checked example answers the exact question negatively; it is not a novelty claim.

his_statement: exact à gauche
statement: On the small category of finite abelian constant coefficients, H^1(X,C)=0 for every C implies that H^2(X,−) is left exact and hence prorepresentable; Artinianity gives strict prorepresentability. computation: Independent long-exact-sequence proof in independent_checks.md §3; no finite computation is advertised as a pi_2 identification.

his_statement: Inertia order invertible gives trace surjective.
statement: Let B be an integral normal commutative ring with finite G action and A=B^G local. If the inertia-group order at a maximal ideal of B is invertible in the corresponding residue field, then Tr_G(B) contains a unit of A, hence1. Every semilinear B-module is cohomologically trivial. The stated normal/integral setup is retained rather than discarded.
computation: CRT chooses an element supported at one maximal ideal; trace there equals |I| times the residue-field trace. Separability makes that field trace nonzero; |I| invertible preserves nonzeroness. The invariant trace lies outside the maximal ideal of A.
fate: This is the tame trace argument: reduce modulo a maximal ideal, sum over the decomposition group, use the separable residue trace and the invertible inertia multiplicity, then lift a nonzero trace and use locality. The manuscript’s assertion is supported by this direct proof and the standard trace/projectivity theorem.

his_statement: Relative trace of an endomorphism equals identity; restriction gives stable elements.
statement: For H≤G finite and a G-module M with id_M=Tr_H^G(φ), φ∈End_H(M), M is relatively H-projective. Restriction on Tate cohomology is injective with image the H-stable elements, and unrestricted corestriction is surjective. Stable means the usual restriction/conjugation equalities on H∩gHg⁻¹.
computation: Weighted transfer satisfies cor φ_* res=id. For a stable class a, the double-coset formula reduces res cor φ_*(a) to (Tr_H^G φ)_*(a)=a. Thus restriction identifies the stable subgroup; cor is onto since every class is cor(φ_*res(class)).
fate: Higman1954, as stated in AKO IV4.2, is the exact relative-projectivity criterion. The cohomological conclusion follows by the weighted transfer cor∘φ_* and the double-coset formula. It must be separated from the false extra claim about corestriction restricted to stable elements. Broué2007§6.8 and the group-algebra example printed55 give the relative trace criterion; its bibliography distinguishes Higman’s1954 Modules with a group of operators (369–376) from Indecomposable representations at characteristic p (377–381). This historical reference does not validate the false stable-corestriction clause.

his_statement: If Gi=1, H¹(G,O×)=0.
statement: For a semilocal commutative ring O with finite G action, transitive on maximal ideals, and trivial inertia at a maximal ideal, the resulting Galois torsor O/O^G gives H¹(G,O×)=Pic(O^G)=0 because O^G is local. his_statement: When can one pass to completion in Tate cohomology?
statement: For A noetherian, G finite acting A-linearly on a finite A-module M, and I-adic completion, Tate cohomology commutes with completion: Hhat^r(G,M)⊗A Ahat≅Hhat^r(G,M⊗A Ahat), all r. The manuscript also proposes decomposition/inertia comparisons and dense-image variants whose full topology is unspecified.
computation: In each Tate degree the complex has a finite direct sum of copies of M. Flat tensor commutes with kernels and images, hence cohomology. Finite generation identifies algebraic tensor with I-adic completion.
fate: Flatness of noetherian completion and a complete resolution with finite free terms give the stated sufficient condition. This settles a concrete version, not the entire undefined density assertion.

his_statement: Even for injective F, sections on a closed Y need not extend to a neighborhood.
statement: For irreducible X with distinct closed points a,b, let F=∏_(x∈X)i_(x)*Q, the injective sheaf of arbitrary Q-valued functions. A closed pushforward from an irreducible curve meeting a line at two points gives the same phenomenon with irreducible Y.

his_statement: Vanishing H¹ on every open is equivalent to vanishing of all higher groups there.
statement: For an abelian sheaf F on any topological space X, H¹(U,F)=0 for every open U iff H^i(U,F)=0 for every open U and all i>0. These imply and are implied by vanishing of positive Čech cohomology for every open cover of every U.
computation: Embed F→I injective. H¹(U,F)=0 makes0→F(U)→I(U)→C(U)→0 exact for every U. Flasqueness of I then makes C flasque, so the two-term flasque resolution gives vanishing in every positive degree.
fate: The argument is the ordinary-space Cartan acyclicity criterion; SGA4 V4.3/V5.9 and Stacks03F9 give the general framework. The source’s cokernel-flasque argument supplies a direct re-proof of the H¹ criterion.

his_statement: The Gysin map is surjective for i≥n+1 and bijective for i≥n+2.
statement: Let X be regular projective of pure dimension n over a separably closed field, Y a regular hyperplane section, and F a locally constant torsion sheaf with orders invertible in the field. Purity and affine Lefschetz make H^(i−2)(Y,F(−1))→H^i(X,F) surjective for i≥n+1 and an isomorphism for i≥n+2. The deleted invertibility condition is necessary for this argument.
computation: For U=X−Y, H^j(U,F)=0 for j>n. In H^(i−1)(U,F)→H_Y^i(X,F)→H^i(X,F)→H^i(U,F), the last term vanishes for i≥n+1, and the first also vanishes for i≥n+2.
fate: SGA4 XIV3.3 is the exact Gysin consequence; relative purity is treated in XVI3.7. The two boundary degrees follow from the localization sequence, not from a convention about the ambiguous H_Y exponent.

his_statement: The two-dimensional tame local lemma, with Abhyankar to be made explicit.
statement: Let A be regular local of dimension2 with regular parameters x,y. A finite normal Galois extension B/A of group order invertible in A, branched only in V(x) and completely split at the generic point of V(y), is étale. After strict henselization and choosing a connected component, tame Abhyankar gives B=A[T]/(T^n−x); splitting modulo y forces n=1.
status_on_pages: proof sketched; external lemma explicitly requested
computation: In A/yA, x is a uniformizer. T^n−x is Eisenstein, hence defines a degree-n field extension of its fraction field. Complete splitting at that generic point is possible only when n=1.
fate: SGA1 X3.6 is the named Abhyankar lemma, and SGA4 XV3 uses it in this smooth-acyclicity proof. The coordinate form requires strict locality and a connected normal component; it is not asserted before those reductions.

his_statement: G only on V; wild ramification complicates local constancy; codimension≥2 causes no trouble.
statement: For i:V=X−Y→X, the Leray spectral sequence R^pf_*(R^qi_*G)⇒R^(p+q)h_*G reduces local constancy to that of its terms. Wild ramification obstructs a naive smooth-boundary theorem. Finite locally constant G extends across codimension≥2 when the ambient scheme is regular and the purity hypotheses hold; codimension alone on a singular normal X does not suffice.
status_on_pages: open on the pages with a qualified purity assertion
computation: Leray bidegrees are(p,q) with total p+q. Extension of a finite locally constant sheaf is equivalent to extension of its finite étale trivializing cover; purity removes a codimension≥2 branch locus only under its regularity assumptions.
fate: SGA1X3.1 gives purity in the regular setting. A precise later controlled wild case is Achinger2017 corollary2.3: for a smooth projective geometrically connected curve family with a section and a finite locally constant F_ℓ-sheaf on its complement, constant Swan conductor at the section makes all ordinary and compactly supported higher direct images locally constant and compatible with base change. Example1.2 exhibits base-change failure for an Artin–Schreier sheaf under A²→A¹ projection. These exact results explain the need to control ramification; they do not settle the manuscript’s unspecified higher-dimensional programme.

his_statement: Noetherian normal rings are Krull; essential valuations are normalized.
statement: For an integral domain A, noetherian plus integrally closed implies Krull. In a Krull domain the essential valuations at height-one primes are normalized discrete valuations and detect membership by v_P(x)≥0. The word domain is necessary and is supplied by the surrounding fraction-field notation.
computation: For an extremal divisor P, the divisorial ideals for P and2P are strictly nested. Choose x in their difference: div(x)≥P but not≥2P, so v_P(x)=1. The uncertain relation must be not≥, not merely≠, for this argument.
fate: The leaf is a reused Bourbaki-style chapterVII typescript. Heinzer–Rotthaus–Wiegand2020§2.11–2.18 states these classical Krull facts. A bibliographic trace identifies Bourbaki Algèbre commutative chapterVII publication1965, but this run does not date the typescript from that publication.

his_statement: The finite intersection of Krull subrings of a field is Krull.
statement: If R1,…,Rn are Krull subrings of a common field F, then S=∩Rj is Krull, even if their fraction fields differ. Restrict all essential valuations to FracS, discard trivial restrictions, normalize the nontrivial discrete value subgroups, and retain finite character because n is finite.
computation: Each restricted value group is0 or a subgroup mZ of Z. Divide bym for normalization. For fixed0≠s∈S only finitely many valuations from each Rj are nonzero, so the union over finitely many j is finite. Membership follows from simultaneous nonnegative valuations.
fate: This is the classical intersection theorem; the valuation definition in Heinzer–Rotthaus–Wiegand2020§2.11 gives exactly the reconstruction used on the typescript. Their§9.7 also uses intersection stability. The draft’s family(v_ji) after defining w_ji is a notational slip to scan-check.

his_statement: Refinement of the questioned residual H¹ comparison (this run).
statement: If O is local Artin, G finite acts on O, and |G| is invertible in O, then H¹(G,O×)→H¹(G,κ×) is an isomorphism. This is a proved sufficient refinement of the source question, not a theorem stated by him; it does not by itself replace G by inertia without taking residual invariance into account.

computation: The filtration1+m^r has successive quotients m^r/m^(r+1), additive G-modules. Multiplication by|G| is invertible, so every positive group-cohomology group of these quotients vanishes. Inductively H¹ and H² of1+m vanish; 1→1+m→O×→κ×→1 then gives the claimed isomorphism.
fate: Standard finite-group averaging and the nilpotent filtration prove this tame Artin-local case. It is explicitly separated from the false wild comparison CL-SA12-456.

his_statement: Refinement of the regular-representation norm argument (this run).
statement: For Γ=(Fℓ)^r, a nontrivial translation in the regular representation has determinant(−1)^((ℓ−1)ℓ^(r−1)). The determinant is identically1 except Γ=C2. For every finite representationρ,ρ⊕det(ρ)^(−1) has determinant1 and remains faithful whenρ is faithful.

his_statement: Restriction of an injective sheaf to a closed subset need not be flasque.
statement: Let X be an irreducible space containing two irreducible closed curves Y1,Y2 meeting only at p, and let I be the sheaf of arbitrary Q-valued functions on X. It is a product of injective skyscraper sheaves. Set Y=Y1∪Y2. The section of I|_(Y−{p}) equal to the constant germ0 on Y1−{p} and1 on Y2−{p} does not extend to Y: an ambient function representing a germ at p would have to be0 and1 on two nonempty intersecting open neighborhoods. Thus I|Y is not flasque.
computation: See outputs/calculations.json#closed_restriction and the full construction in CL-SA12-475–476. The all-functions sheaf on the ambient irreducible component is injective; the incompatible0/1 germs arise after restriction to the closed reducible intersection.
fate: The manuscript gives an explicit germ obstruction; general sheaf references confirm that inverse image need not preserve injectives or flasqueness. The exact ambient two-branch configuration and restriction maps are retained in the proof certificate, not replaced by an assertion that the sheaf of all functions itself is nonflasque.

computation: New independent counterexample: X=A¹_C, Λ=Fℓ, and F=⊕_{m∈Z}i_{m*}Λ for the closed integer points. On the quasi-compact algebraic étale site, a section of the sheaf direct sum is supported in finitely many summands, so H0(X,F)=⊕_ZΛ. Analytification preserves colimits; the integer set is closed discrete in C, so arbitrary choices at all integer points are locally finite sections of the analytic direct sum, giving H0(Xan,Fan)=∏_ZΛ. The comparison is the strict direct-sum inclusion. All sheaves are killed byℓ and X is smooth affine finite type; F is not constructible. This argument uses no numerical computation.
